title: Recording: Hey Diddle, A Love For You by Paul McCartney | 1970
content:
Studio B, CBS Studio Building, New York City
Producer: Paul McCartney

Although part of the sessions for the Paul and Linda McCartney album Ram, on 26 October 1970 two outtakes were worked on: ‘Hey Diddle’ and ‘A Love For You’.

‘Hey Diddle’ was initially titled ‘She Can’t Be Found’. It remained unreleased until it appeared at the end of the 2001 compilation Wingspan: Hits And History, alongside a home recording of ‘Bip Bop’

In understanding how lyrics come about, you have to appreciate the stage of life of the writer. Today, I might write totally differently, but when you have little kids, as I did at this time, you’re often composing ditties like ‘Her Majesty’ or ‘Hey Diddle’ or something like this.

You’re just not sitting there trying to be too meaningful. I used to do these little songs just to amuse the kids. But the truth is I still write for kids. Maybe it means I’ve never fully grown up, but I’ve got one that’s called ‘The Bouncy Song’, and one, I confess, called ‘Running Around The Room’, which is another family classic. Then we have one that goes, ‘Fishes, fishes, fishes swimming in the sea’. There are quite a few of them from when the kids were growing up – songs I didn’t release.

Paul McCartney
The Lyrics: 1956 To The Present

Following a break for lunch, McCartney led the session musicians – guitarist Hugh McCracken and drummer Denny Seiwell – through ‘A Love For You’. It remained incomplete, but recording continued the following day.

McCartney reportedly planned to issue the song as a single, with ‘Get On The Right Thing’ on the b-side, but it was cancelled after the formation of Wings.

The recording was revived in October 1980 during the final Wings days, at Rude Studio in Campbeltown, Scotland, while McCartney was working on the abandoned Cold Cuts project. The overdubs included guitar by Laurence Juber and percussion by Steve Holley.

Further work took place at Hog Hill Mill in September 1986, and the track was mixed by engineer Jon Kelly.

‘A Love For You’ remained in the archives until 2002, when film producer Ralph Sall asked McCartney if he had a song that could be used in the soundtrack of The In-Laws, a remake of the 1979 film of the same name.

McCartney agreed, and added more guitar at Henson Recording Studios in Los Angeles. It was mixed by Sall and David Kahne, the producer of Driving Rain.

Although The In-Laws was a box office bomb, ‘A Love For You’ appeared over the end credits. The soundtrack contained two other McCartney songs: Wings’ ‘I’m Carrying’ and a previously-unreleased version of ‘Live And Let Die’.

Jon Kelly’s 1986 mix of ‘A Love For You’ was included on the 2012 reissue of Ram.
